subject: FastRetail capacity & latency follow-up — deployment-mode recommendations
messages:

Subject: Re: Discovery — throughput/latency needs (FastRetail)

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick written recap from my side so we have a single source of truth: 
- Production traffic today: average 70 QPS, typical peak 250 QPS during daytime retail hours.
- Spiky events: we expect one-off spikes up to ~300 QPS for promotions (Black Friday-like load is a separate program).
- Latency target: P95 <= 150ms for single-turn completions on our typical 512-token prompts (we can stretch to 200ms for complex flows but want to avoid >250ms).
- Data & compliance: logs stored for 90 days, must be able to restrict dataset export; SOC2 + ISO27001 required.
- Procurement: need SOW + rough monthly cost estimate to start legal review.

I've attached our internal latency profile (FR_RTO_latency_report.pdf). Can you confirm whether hosted API can meet the P95 target at peak, and if not what Dedicated/reserved configuration you'd recommend? Also what burst model do you recommend for short spikes?

Thanks — Amelia
Amelia Park

Subject: Re: Discovery — throughput/latency needs (FastRetail)

Amelia — thanks for the writeup and the attachment, very helpful. Short version up front: we can support your P95 target with multiple deployment approaches, but the right trade-off depends on how predictable your peaks are and whether you want to commit to reserved baseline capacity. I outlined options below and a suggested next-step benchmark plan.

Option A — Hosted API (fastest onboarding)
- Pros: immediate start, no infra procurement; autoscaling for unpredictable spikes; built-in SOC2 controls on hosted tier.
- Cons: cost can be variable at sustained high QPS; P95 at peak depends on request distribution and batching benefits — our test suggests ~140–170ms for profiles similar to yours at 250 QPS (with standard batching).

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended if peaks predictable)
- Pros: predictable throughput, lower unit cost, optimized kernel selection and sustained P95 improvements (we can target ~110–140ms at 250 QPS depending on model variant and quantization). Supports autoscaling rules you control within the pool.
- Cons: requires monthly commit; lead time to provision reserved pools can be 7–10 days for the initial capacity.

Option C — Private VPC / On-prem
- Pros: lowest single-tenant latency if colocated with your infra; full network isolation.
- Cons: longer setup, procurement/ops overhead, usually only worthwhile for steady, very latency-sensitive workloads.

Burst strategy we recommend: baseline Dedicated capacity sized to handle 200–220 QPS sustained, with hosted fallback for spikes above baseline. This keeps unit cost low and preserves availability for short high bursts (autofallback routing is automatic in our platform). For Black Friday-level capacity we typically run a temporary reserved capacity uplift with a short-term commitment.

Benchmark plan (recommended next steps)
1) 7-day hosted pilot with your representative workloads (we'll run in our dev cluster) — measure P50/P95 and CPU/GPU utilization.
2) Parallel Dedicated sizing run: we provision a short-term dedicated pool (14 days) sized to 225 QPS baseline to validate P95 targets and cost delta.
3) Produce an SOW & cost estimate for procurement based on the dedicated run.

Attachments I will share after the pilot: redwood_estimate.csv and a draft SOW. If that sounds good, can we lock a pilot start date next Monday (2027-05-03)? Please confirm procurement timeline for the SOW.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Irene — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed, thank you. A couple of clarifications from the infra/procurement side: 
- Procurement note: we need the SOW and an estimated monthly burn to start legal review; target to have internal review completed by 2027-05-05.
- Spikes: promotional bursts are usually 10–30 minutes and happen ~2–3 times per month. For Black Friday we will plan a separate uplift (likely multi-week).
- P95 tolerance: we can accept 150ms for standard flows; anything consistently above 180ms would be a blocker. 

We can commit to a hosted pilot starting 2027-05-03 for the 7-day run. For the dedicated sizing run, procurement would prefer a 14-day trial that can be treated as an evaluation invoice rather than a long-term commit — is that feasible? Also please attach the cost estimate and SOW draft so I can circulate.

Thanks — Amelia

Great — thanks for confirming the pilot window. TL;DR: we can do a two-phased evaluation that minimizes your risk and gives procurement the outputs they need. Details below and action items.

Phase 1 — Hosted pilot (2027-05-03 to 2027-05-09)
- Redwood provides a hosted environment with your workload replayed. We capture P50/P95/P99, token cost, and cache hit rates.
- Deliverables: pilot report, raw metrics, and redwood_estimate.csv.
- No commitment required.

Phase 2 — Dedicated sizing trial (proposed 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-23)
- Short-term dedicated pool provisioned as an evaluation invoice (14 days). We size baseline to 220–240 QPS to validate P95 <= 150ms target and look at cost per 1M tokens vs hosted.
- Deliverables: SOW draft, monthly estimate for baseline commit, recommended autoscaling/burst policy (we'll include a fallback to hosted).

Mutual action plan (milestones & owners)
- 2027-04-28: Redwood sends SOW draft + cost estimate (owner: Irene).
- 2027-05-01: FastRetail confirms pilot credentials and test dataset + any redaction rules (owner: Luis/Amelia).
- 2027-05-03: Hosted pilot starts (owner: Irene/Aditya).
- 2027-05-10: Provision dedicated trial (owner: Redwood ops).
- 2027-05-24: Post-trial review and procurement decision (owner: FastRetail + Redwood sales).

Questions for procurement/legal to help us speed review:
1) Any special contractual language around data residency or logging beyond standard SOC2/ISO?
2) Do you require IP clauses for evaluation workloads?

I've attached the SOW draft (SOW_draft_v2.docx) and the latency profile you sent is included as FR_RTO_latency_report.pdf. We'll upload the pilot measurement dashboard to the HubSpot deal and share the link.

Can we lock a 30-minute sync for Monday 2027-05-03 at 10:00am PT to kick off the pilot? If so, I'll send a calendar invite and the credentials.

Best,
